    {"name": "value_for_money_perception", "supports_focus": false, "rationale": "Redundant with price_value_alignment."}
  ],
  "focus_coherence": 0.85,
  "structure_quality": 0.55,
  "focus_actionability": 0.8,
  "rationale": "The columns collectively centre on one coherent, data-inferable focus: the facets driving overall airline passenger experience/satisfaction (crew, seat, food, aircraft, operations, ground, value, consistency). This is an actionable framing an analyst could investigate to identify which aspect most affects Overall Rating/Recommended. Focus coherence is strong. However, structure quality is weakened by substantial redundancy: roughly five facets are duplicated near-verbatim (aircraft condition, operational disruption, service consistency, ground/check-in, value for money), so the added set is padded with restated columns rather than a clean, differentiated facet decomposition. Several facets (seat, food, value) also merely re-encode existing original numeric ratings as categoricals, adding limited new granularity. The core inferred focus is sound and useful, but the executed structure is inflated and not cleanly parsimonious."
}
